summary: This script loads environment variables from a .env file and then prints out two of those variables (a full name and email address). It's a simple way to read configuration from a file without polluting the shell's environment with temporary variables.

explanations.3: set -o allexport tells bash to automatically export every variable that gets defined, so when we source the .env file, all its variables become available to any commands we run next.
explanations.4: source .env reads and executes the .env file in the current shell, loading all the variables defined in it.
explanations.5: set +o allexport turns off automatic exporting, so any new variables created after this point won't be exported — we're cleaning up after ourselves.
